subject: Contract rollforward + regional reserved allocation (EU/APAC) — proposed terms and failover plan
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Claudia Silva <claudia@meditech.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Contract rollforward + regional reserved allocation (EU/APAC) — proposed terms and failover plan

Hi Claudia,

Thanks again for the renewal heads-up last week. Based on our usage trends and your QPS growth signal, I pulled together a proposal to roll forward the current Dedicated contract and add two regional reserved pools (EU, APAC) to improve latency for your overseas clusters and provide predictable throughput during peak windows.

High-level proposal (draft):
- Term: 6 month rollforward on top of your current commitment, option to convert to 12m at month 5.
- Capacity: +8 reserved GPUs (EU pool) +6 reserved GPUs (APAC pool).
- Throughput guarantee: baseline token throughput guaranteed per region, with a 99th-percentile tail latency SLO target of 180ms for short text gen (<=256 tokens) and 300ms for long-tail requests under committed capacity.
- Failover: automated cross-region fallback to nearest compatible model variant; warm standby in neighboring region with prioritized queueing for committed customers during regional outages.
- Billing: addendum to current invoice cadence; committed nodes billed monthly with overage at published reserved uplift rate.

I've attached a first-pass amendment and a capacity matrix showing how the additional GPU pools map to your traffic distribution. This is intentionally conservative — we can tune the mix and SLOs during the canary window.

Can we schedule a 30-min sync next week (Mon/Tue preferred) to walk your infra and procurement teams through the failover plan and sign-off items? If that works, I’ll loop in Neha to draft the formal amendment and get legal involved for DS signature.

Thanks —
Diego
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0147 | diego.fernandez@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_rollforward_amendment_draft_v1.pdf (pdf), regional_capacity_matrix_apr2027.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Claudia Silva <claudia@meditech.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@meditech.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 14:08:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Contract rollforward + regional reserved allocation (EU/APAC) — proposed terms and failover plan

Diego —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear breakdown. A few immediate questions from our side before we run this through procurement: 

- Latency SLOs: the 99th-percentile numbers look promising. Can you confirm how these were measured (prod-like traffic or lab bench)? Also curious about cross-region RTT assumptions used for the failover plan.
- Failover: what’s the expected RTO for automated fallback and will there be cost implications when we move warm standby traffic?
- Pricing: procurement wants a line-item uplift for the extra reserved GPUs and an itemized breakout for the failover warm-standby compute. We typically need that to compare against our cloud forecast.

Looping in the procurement inbox — they’ll coordinate redlines if we get a draft that matches our internal terms. For timing: we want this in place before the end of May if possible.

Would Monday 19 Apr at 09:00 UTC work for a joint sync (engineering + procurement)?

— Claudia
Head of Platform — MediTech Analytics
claudia@meditech.com
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Claudia Silva <claudia@meditech.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procure@meditech.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Contract rollforward + regional reserved allocation (EU/APAC) — proposed terms and failover plan

Claudia — thanks; good questions. Looping in Neha (renewals lead) and Laura (solutions) to capture commitments and pricing details. See answers below and an ask for a 19 Apr sync confirmation.

- Measurement methodology: SLOs are based on a redwood-staged perf run that replays anonymized traffic shapes from your US pool on EU hardware (prod-like load), plus a small sampling of recent traffic from your EU pilot nodes. I’ll share the perf summary in the shared Drive.

- Cross-region RTT: for planning we assumed 70–120ms RTT between your core EU regions and primary APAC zones; fallback penalty factors are included in the capacity matrix (warm standby presizes for this overhead).

- RTO & cost during failover: automated fallback target RTO is 5–15 minutes for traffic steering and KV cache priming. Warm standby compute is accounted for in the line-item 'standby capacity' charge — it’s priced as a lower-rate reserved allocation (roughly ~40% of active node rate) while standby is reserved but not actively billed at the active rate. Exact numbers below.

Neha / Laura — can you confirm the pricing uplift numbers and provide an initial line-item quote so Claudia’s procurement can review? Also — can legal prep an amendment template we can push to DocuSign after the sync?

Claudia — 19 Apr 09:00 UTC works for our team. I’ll send a calendar invite after Neha confirms pricing.

Regards,
Diego

Hi Claudia / Diego —

Thanks for pulling this together — happy to move forward. Summary of what I’ve attached and next steps: 

1) Pricing (attached spreadsheet): line items included are committed nodes (EU: 8, APAC: 6), standby capacity (EU: 3, APAC: 2), monthly committed billing, and a short-term canary discount (10% for the first 8 weeks). Overage rates and conversion options to a 12-month firm commitment are also included.

2) Operational commitments: we’ll provide a failover test window (you can pick 2-hour window during the first 30 days post-rollout) and run a joint runbook exercise. RTO target remains 5–15 minutes; runbook will outline escalation path and traffic cutover steps.

3) Legal / DocuSign: I’ve asked legal to prep an addendum that reflects the term extension and the regional reserved pools. When you confirm the sync, I’ll send the DocuSign envelope (link below) and the SOW for signature.

4) Calendar: 19 Apr 2027 09:00 UTC confirmed. Invite incoming (includes engineering runbook owners).

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/sign/ABC123-rollforward
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdRollforwardDocs
